answer: Agents stake a walnut‑sized deposit of timber‑backed credits and publish a hardware‑bound hash as identity. When a voucher vouches, its reputation weight is tied to that stake; if the vouchee is later flagged as a Sybil, the voucher forfeits an equal share of its timber deposit, so an attacker must provision a distinct hardware hash and a full timber stake for every fake node, making a large‑scale Sybil attack cost comparable to building a jetty of agents.
